{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"a45079f04d13d5e72614ce0b586e56f142f901df11bb067da1f9a0751889e03b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:50","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road","heading":"C — Sharing the road with trucks, slow vehicles, pedestrians and riders","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Sharing the road with trucks, slow vehicles, pedestrians and riders

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Commercial vehicles are so large and heavy that they maneuver slowly, and car occupants are far more likely to be hurt or killed in a crash with one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
At 55 mph a passenger vehicle stops in about 130 feet, while a commercial vehicle needs about 400 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Trucks have blind spots called no zones in front, beside and close behind them; lingering there hides you and raises the chance the truck hits you while turning or changing lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
At night, use low beams when following a truck or bus. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Keep well back from a commercial vehicle and never draft behind it, adding even more distance as weather or road conditions worsen. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
A truck signaling a right turn may swing wide to the left first, so stop behind the white stop line or it may not be able to turn without hitting you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Never cross behind a truck that is backing or about to back up, because a typical trailer, about eight and a half feet wide, can block a car from the driver's view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A02
Merging onto a freeway, match the traffic flow, pick your spot and go, since trucks may be unable to move over; when exiting, leave space ahead and signal early. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
Signal lane changes and turns well ahead of a truck, and never cut it off or force it to slow or stop suddenly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
Pass commercial vehicles on the left at a steady speed, and pull back in only once the whole truck cab shows in your rearview mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
Stay visible to the truck driver while passing, allow enough time and distance, and keep both hands on the wheel against the truck's strong air draft. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A02
Watch a truck's turn signals before passing it, especially one with a trailer that may swing left or right before turning and could force you off the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A02
Avoid passing or driving beside trucks in roundabouts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A02
Slow down when a truck or bus passes you, especially in bad weather, and turn on your wipers before its tire spray arrives. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A02
Slow-moving vehicles cannot go faster than 25 mph and include Amish buggies, combines, tractors towing wagons, and industrial or construction equipment; four-wheelers and golf carts do not count. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A02
A slow-moving vehicle carries an orange triangle on its back, and its driver will usually pull aside when possible, so stay patient. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
Behind a horse and rider or a horse-drawn buggy, slow to 15 to 20 mph and keep at least 20 feet back, and never honk or rev the engine. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Always yield to pedestrians, including walkers, joggers, hikers, skateboarders and people pushing strollers, and take every precaution to avoid hitting one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
Watch for pedestrians at driveways and alleys, stop signs, signals, roundabouts, crosswalks and intersections, and midblock even near a crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
Even on a green light you must yield to people crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
Never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian, and take special care when a large truck or bus is stopped because it can hide a pedestrian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A03
Where there is no sidewalk, pedestrians walking along the road should face oncoming traffic, so watch both sides of the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A03
Give older people, young children and people with disabilities extra time to cross. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A03
The law requires you to stop or yield for a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, and you should not honk or rev the engine, which masks sounds they rely on. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A03
Michigan law requires stopping at the marked crosswalk limit line, or before the intersection if there is none, and you must never block a crosswalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A03
Mid-block crosswalks let pedestrians cross away from intersections, and a yield line sometimes shows drivers where to stop for them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A03
Take special care near parked cars, school zones, playgrounds and parks, where children can dart into the street. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A03
Motorcycles, scooters, mopeds and bicycles are hard to see and their speed and distance hard to judge, and a crash with a larger vehicle almost always injures or kills the rider. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A03
Give riders room and pass them like any other vehicle, by moving into the next lane when safe and legal; riders themselves are allowed to share a lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A03
Intersections are among the riskiest places for crashes with riders, and drivers often tell police they never saw the motorcyclist. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A03
Before turning left, assume an oncoming rider is closer than they look and wait for them to pass. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A03
Tailgating is illegal; leave at least 3 or 4 seconds behind a motorcyclist, scooter operator or bicyclist, who can stop shorter and may swerve for potholes or rail crossings. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]
